Rossi Secures Funding for Westmoreland County Projects
September 15, 2026
WESTMORELAND COUNTY -
Rep. Leslie Rossi (R-Westmoreland) today announced more than $3.2 million in Local Share Account (LSA) grants have been approved by the Commonwealth Financing Authority (CFA) to support critical infrastructure improvements, public safety, municipal operations and community projects across Westmoreland County.
Local Share Account grants are funded through gaming revenues under Act 71 of 2004 and are used to support economic development, community improvement and other projects that enhance the quality of life for Pennsylvania residents.
“These grants are about making smart investments that deliver results for the people of Westmoreland County,” said Rossi. “Whether it’s replacing failing infrastructure, improving roads and wastewater systems, equipping our first responders or helping municipalities keep up with essential services, these projects address our needs and will strengthen the 59th District for years to come.”
The approved projects for the 59th District include:
•	Bolivar Borough - $656,000
to replace the borough’s deteriorated, more than 100-year-old clay storm sewer system around Market Street. The project will install properly sized trunk lines, laterals and inlets to address flooding, sinkholes, roadway icing and property damage. LSA funds will be used for construction, engineering and administrative costs.
•	City of Latrobe - $461,857
to design, permit and construct a new bioretention pond as part of the city’s Pollution Reduction Plan. The project will treat stormwater runoff from approximately 45 acres of residential development, reduce pollutant loads entering Loyalhanna Creek and help reduce downstream flooding and peak flows. LSA funds will be used for infrastructure, engineering and administrative costs.
•	Cook Township - $54,082
to purchase a new excavator for municipal maintenance projects. The new equipment will replace aging machinery that is increasingly expensive to repair and will allow the township to complete necessary work more efficiently.
•	Cook Township - $142,500
to resurface Armel Hollow Road, a main roadway through the municipality that has experienced deterioration from daily traffic and extreme weather. LSA funds will be used for construction costs.
•	Derry Borough - $147,361
to improve the sanitary sewer system by installing and upsizing sections of sewer line, retrofitting existing manholes and completing roadway restoration. The improvements will increase system capacity and reduce the risk of flooding caused by inflow and infiltration. LSA funds will be used for construction, engineering and administrative costs.
•	Derry Township Municipal Authority - $217,233
for improvements to several pump stations and the authority’s office and shop. The project includes roof replacement, a new alarm dialer system, software upgrades, a wet well aeration system and emergency generator and transfer switch installations to improve reliability and continuity of operations. LSA funds will be used for construction, engineering and administrative costs.
•	Donegal Borough - $500,000
to construct a complete public sanitary sewer system to replace failing on-lot septic systems. The project will install approximately 10,910 feet of gravity sewer, 1,871 feet of force main and two pump stations, eliminating untreated sewage discharges, protecting water quality and removing a public health hazard. LSA funds will be used for construction, engineering and administrative costs.
•	Donegal Township - $114,435
to construct an addition to the township office building to provide dedicated office space for two officials and improve public access to township services.
•	Ligonier Borough - $367,500
to replace the outdated restroom facility at Friendship Park with a modern, fully accessible building that meets current codes and visitor needs. The project also includes utility upgrades and an accessible route connecting the parking area and playground to the restrooms. LSA funds will be used for renovation, engineering and administrative costs.
•	Ligonier Township - $200,000
to purchase a new 10-ton dump/plow truck equipped with a dump body, spreader and snowplow kit. The new vehicle will replace an aging 2001 truck and improve road maintenance, snow removal and public safety operations.
•	Mount Pleasant Township - $254,081
to purchase a new Mack municipal truck and associated equipment. The vehicle will replace an existing truck that has reached the end of its useful life and requires costly ongoing repairs.
•	Seward Borough, on behalf of the Volunteer Fire Department and Relief Association of Seward - $53,316
to purchase a UTV, rescue skid and rescue trailer for brush-fire response and search and rescue operations in surrounding state game lands.
•	St. Clair Township - $65,000
to purchase a new tractor with a boom mower for road maintenance, storm sewer work, hauling materials and maintaining sight lines along township roads. The new equipment will replace a vehicle that has reached the end of its useful life.
The Commonwealth Financing Authority is an independent agency responsible for administering state investments that promote economic growth, infrastructure development and community revitalization throughout Pennsylvania.

title: Westmoreland County House Delegation Works to Better Protect Citizens from Juvenile Sex Offenders
raw_text:
Westmoreland County House Delegation Works to Better Protect Citizens from Juvenile Sex Offenders
June 11, 2026
GREENSBURG
– Westmoreland County House members today announced they plan to introduce legislation to improve public safety, strengthen oversight of high-risk sexual offenders and reform Pennsylvania’s management of individuals discharged from the Sexual Responsibility and Treatment Program (SRTP). The legislators are Reps. Eric Nelson (R-Westmoreland), Eric Davanzo (R-Westmoreland), Leslie Rossi (R-Westmoreland), Abby Major (R-Armstrong/Westmoreland), Jill Cooper (R-Westmoreland) and Brian Rasel (R-Westmoreland).
SRTP is a specialized, secure treatment program operated by the Department of Human Services at Torrance State Hospital in Westmoreland County. The program serves sexually violent delinquent children, a narrowly defined category of juvenile sexual offenders who have been adjudicated delinquent for serious sexual offenses and subsequently determined by a court to suffer from a mental abnormality or personality disorder that makes them likely to engage in predatory sexual offenses.
The bill is in response to significant concerns that have been raised regarding the discharge process, the lack of uniform registration and notification requirements, community placement decisions, and the concentration of placement responsibilities in a single county.
“Only sexually violent delinquent children adjudicated after December 2012 are subject to lifetime sexual offender registration requirements,” the delegation said. “This creates a troubling inconsistency in our laws and a substantial number of individuals confined in the SRTP for serious sexual offenses committed before that date may ultimately be discharged into the community without any ongoing registration obligation. It should be stated that Torrance State Hospital nor its staff are to blame.”
The lawmakers also noted individuals discharged from the SRTP are subject to a one-year outpatient treatment and supervision program following their release. According to the law each county is responsible for all aspects of the commitment and recommitment process, as well as providing aftercare for individuals from their respective counties. However, lawmakers have been notified that a concentration of offenders is being placed in Westmoreland County despite them coming from areas across the state.
“No single county should bear a disproportionate share of the responsibility for managing individuals discharged from a statewide treatment program for sexual offenders,” they said. “A single year of community-based supervision is also insufficient to ensure a successful transition to independent living. The period immediately following discharge is the most critical time for monitoring compliance with treatment, evaluating behavioral adjustment and identifying emerging risk factors.”
The bill would require:
•
All individuals discharged from the SRTP to be subject to lifetime sexual offender registration and oversight requirements, regardless of when they were adjudicated delinquent.
•
All counties to participate in the placement process and assist in identifying appropriate housing and support services for individuals discharged from the SRTP who are returning to their communities.
•
The establishment of a network of supervised transitional homes throughout Pennsylvania designed specifically for individuals discharged from the SRTP.
•
The extension of the required outpatient treatment and supervision period from one year to two years. The additional year will provide treatment professionals and supervising authorities with greater opportunities to monitor progress and facilitate a safer and more gradual reintegration into communities.
The group met with stakeholders, including the Sexual Offenders Assessment Board, the Department of Human Services, SRTP officials and Westmoreland County Behavioral Health and Developmental Services. This legislation is a product of those meetings.
“There are reasonable and simple expectations on the part of residents throughout Westmoreland County that those who are convicted of crimes will be punished and that adequate protections and transparency requirements are in place upon a criminal’s release,” the delegation said. “The details around this situation strike at the heart of those expectations and the General Assembly can and should take immediate action.”
Several of the lawmakers announced the planned legislation Thursday at a press conference at Twin Lakes Park.

These improvements will increase safety, accessibility, and environmental protection for the surrounding natural areas, including MWA's Rasler Run property.
The GTRP, which is funded through the Marcellus Legacy Fund established under Act 13 of 2012, provides essential support for the planning, development, and enhancement of public parks, trails, greenways, and other recreational spaces across Pennsylvania.
